distribution.reason: LGPL-2.0-or-later crates (sequoia-openpgp, buffered-reader) are linked into the shipped module/binaries without completed corresponding-source, notice or relinking delivery; whole-image licensing, Rust runtime/source reachability, generated layers and digest-bound source delivery remain incomplete. No publication authorized.

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc 2.41. Both channels build cargo build --locked --offline --release --package siguldry --package siguldry-pkcs11 --jobs 2 with Rust 1.98.1 from the digest-pinned toolchain image and 479 hash-verified registry crates reconstructed into a sealed directory source. No patches, no simulation.

Dynamic system OpenSSL and SQLite: the module, binaries and supervisor use Debian base libcrypto.so.3, libssl.so.3 and libsqlite3.so.0 (OpenSSL 3.5.7, SQLite 3.46.1; sqlx sqlite-unbundled). No source-built crypto, no openssl CLI and no legacy provider module in the runtime; ldd receipts identify actual usage.

Co-located supervised signing stack: siguldry-bridge, siguldry-signer, siguldry-server and siguldry-client proxy (bind mode) run as direct supervisor children for the operation/application lifetime. No permanent server/server-ready operation is needed; the preferred proxy daemon runs through the same exec.

Fixed loopback topology: bridge listens on 127.0.0.1:44333 (servers) and 127.0.0.1:44334 (clients); signer and proxy use private sockets under /run/p11lab/siguldry. Each independent shard/client owns its volume, container, PID namespace and network namespace. A second stack cannot share the ports (native bind refusal); no host/shared networking.

mTLS is bootstrapped at runtime by a P11Lab-owned libcrypto helper in the supervisor (RSA-2048, SHA-256, 3650-day validity, SAN+EKU leaves, v3_ca CA), mirroring the vetted upstream devel script semantics without shipping it. Fixed internal identities: server siguldry-server, bridge localhost, user siguldry-client (client CN must equal the username). No baked credentials or initialized state ship; the CA private key is never written.

P11LAB_LABEL defaults to P11Lab, 1..32 ASCII letters/digits/spaces/dot/underscore/hyphen. The label names the single server-side P-256 signing key and therefore the single token (slot 0, token-present index 0). Exactly one key exists; native readiness requires exactly one token-present slot.

First init requires caller key-password input of 32..200 printable ASCII characters via P11LAB_PIN_FILE or P11LAB_PIN (single-line/4096-byte common checks run first). The lower bound is native (user_password_length=32); the token 64..128 PIN-length claim is informational and unenforced. The PIN unlocks the server key through C_Login; the key password travels by anonymous pipe and a private unlinked control file, never argv, logs or markers.

No security-officer input exists: native C_Login(CKU_SO) is CKR_USER_TYPE_INVALID and C_InitToken/C_InitPIN/C_SetPIN are CKR_FUNCTION_NOT_SUPPORTED (0x54). P11LAB_SO_PIN/P11LAB_SO_PIN_FILE inputs are refused when set. C_GenerateKeyPair/C_GenerateKey/C_CreateObject/C_DestroyObject are likewise 0x54; general-token is falsified.

Native connection behavior is preserved: a failed unlock or a sign without login (C_SignInit OK then C_Sign CKR_FUNCTION_FAILED 0x06) breaks that process proxy connection, so later calls in the same process keep failing; fresh processes are unaffected and there is no server lockout. A wrong PIN returns CKR_PIN_INCORRECT (0xA0). No retry, PIN replacement, error translation or semantic patch is added.

Existing init validates static state and native readiness and ignores changed input credential files. Static exact-byte marker/config checks, .init-lock, an exclusive volume lease, private control lock, credential roster, SQLite magic, ownership/mode/link checks run before any native process. The native stack sets the database mode 0640 explicitly (umask-independent); 0600/0640 are accepted for that file only and the 0700 directory remains the boundary. Missing, partial, foreign, incompatible and occupied state is refused. No reset, reprovisioning or state-changing retry is implicit.

init/health/exec use the P11Lab C supervisor: direct service children, real readiness gating (owned PIDs, both sockets, both TCP ports, bounded native whoami, native slot/label/flags/ECDSA check), bounded startup and 64-KiB log sinks, required-service death monitoring, signal forwarding, TERM/KILL escalation and subreaper/adopted-child cleanup. Readiness never logs in; unlocking stays caller authentication.

Persistent keys and key passwords survive clean restart; unlock state does not (each process logs in again). Reset is explicit caller removal/replacement of disposable state after all operations stop. Crash/power-loss recovery is unqualified.

Basic runtime contains no checker, Python, datasets, tracing, compiler, Cargo, OpenSC/pkcs11-tool, openssl CLI or upstream administration scripts. Consumer/checker/proxy derivatives are separate test artifacts with independent identity and admission. A shared network never makes the native module remotely loadable.

signing means exactly the proven narrow observation: pre-provisioned single P-256 key, caller-PIN unlock, ECDSA sign-only with independent OpenSSL original/altered-message oracles. Wider mechanisms, key types, session objects, concurrent clients, other architectures/libcs, hardware security and production mTLS practices (systemd-creds, cert rotation/revocation) are unqualified.

Distribution is blocked independently of crypto or lifecycle outcomes. Linked LGPL-2.0-or-later code (sequoia-openpgp 2.4.1, buffered-reader 1.4.1) has no completed corresponding-source, notice or relinking delivery; twelve locked crates carry manifest-only license declarations; base-package source obligations, Rust standard-library and actual-layer review remain pending.
